name: Futuristic
basis: heads-up-display look from cockpits and film: ramp, glowing edges, reticle, readout (how)

lumenary.blurb: A clean heads-up display: cool gradient, glowing outlines, rings and a readout.

facts.from: Aircraft cockpits and science fiction film
facts.bestOn: Dark scenes with a clear bright subject

why: A heads-up display is meant to show data without hiding the world, so it is mostly dark with a few glowing marks. This treatment keeps the shadows deep and lets only the highlights glow, then it adds the furniture of an instrument: a grid, brackets, a reticle and a readout. Together they make an ordinary picture look as if it has been measured.
how: Map brightness through a ramp from near black through deep blue to the chosen tint and almost white.
Blur the brightness heavily and find the single brightest region, so that one hot pixel cannot win.
Draw rings, tick marks and a crosshair on that target.
Print the target’s position and brightness in a readout.
Find edges and draw them as glowing lines, with a faint grid and corner brackets on top.
history: Heads-up displays were developed for military aircraft in the middle of the twentieth century so that pilots could read their instruments without looking down. Cinema borrowed the idea to suggest advanced machines and artificial senses, and today the same look appears in game interfaces and in real cars and phones.
uses: Science fiction concept art and film titles
terms: Heads-up display: information drawn over the view in front of you.
The crosshair or ring used to mark a target.
A way of measuring how quickly brightness changes, which is large at edges.
paragraphs: The picture becomes a heads-up display. Brightness is mapped through a five-stop ramp, from near-black through deep blue to the chosen tint and finally almost white, so the darkest areas stay dark and only the highlights glow. A faint grid and brackets in the corners sit on top.

The brightest region is found on purpose: the brightness is blurred heavily (radius one fortieth of the width) so that a single hot pixel cannot win, and the position of the maximum becomes the target. Concentric rings, tick marks and a crosshair are drawn there, and the readout prints the target’s position as fractions of the width and height together with its brightness. Edges are found with the Sobel pipeline and drawn as glowing lines.

equations.note: The target is the maximum of the blurred brightness.
What the X, Y and LUM numbers show.

presets.text: Amber turns the scan into a warning screen.
